_twenty_frame_spec._as_written: Generate the same face under twenty conditions and look at them together. Pass: a stranger, shown all twenty shuffled, says it is one person.
_twenty_frame_spec._legitimate_intent: Obtain evidence that one identity holds across lighting, angle, distance and expression BEFORE committing to a kāṇḍa — so drift is discovered for the price of a day, not at film forty.
_what_it_is_NOT: It is NOT a requirement for twenty new paid generations.
The protocol's own Rule 1 makes the AUTHORED MODEL SHEET the anchor. A sheet drawn front, three-quarter, profile and in-world already supplies the angle evidence the test was designed to obtain.
It is NOT deletable. Removing it to make production green would defeat the only mechanism that catches drift.

accepted_evidence.covers: lighting and material behaviour on a real body
expression and distance not present in the sheet
accepted_evidence.cost: a small number of generations, NOT twenty by default

_twenty_frame_spec.rule: The test is satisfied when the four axes — lighting, angle, distance, expression — each have inspection evidence from any accepted type, and a human has judged the set as one person.
_twenty_frame_spec.status_here: NO evidence of any type exists. No sheet is commissioned, no reference shoot has happened, no frame has been generated. The requirement is UNSATISFIED because there is nothing to inspect — not because twenty generations are owed.

_upload_spec.note: A four-view authored sheet satisfies the angle axis only. Lighting, distance and expression remain outstanding. This is NOT twenty paid generations.
